outcome: Intervention rates (induction, artificial rupture of membranes, epidural, oxytocin, episiotomy)
Mode of delivery (cesarean, operative vaginal, spontaneous vaginal)
Maternal outcomes (third- or fourth-degree laceration, postpartum hemorrhage, blood transfusion, severe maternal morbidity)
Newborn outcomes (shoulder dystocia, 5-minute Apgar score less than 7, resuscitation at delivery, birth trauma, neonatal intensive care unit admission)
cohort: Women with low-risk pregnancies delivering singletons at 37 0/7-42 6/7 weeks of gestation at 11 hospitals between 2014 and 2018
finding: In low-risk pregnancies, midwifery care during labor was associated with decreased interventions, lower rates of cesarean and operative vaginal births, and an increased risk of shoulder dystocia in multiparous women.
mod_finding: Midwifery care was associated with an approximately 30% lower risk of cesarean delivery in nulliparous patients and an approximately 40% lower risk in multiparous patients compared to obstetrician care.
